channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: US Announces Location for Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks
item.description: The United States has announced the location for upcoming peace talks between Russia and Ukraine. A trilateral meeting is expected to take place within the next two weeks in one of two countries, following discussions held recently in Saint Petersburg.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Food Inflation Continues to Slow Down, Ministry Reports
item.description: Food inflation in Kazakhstan has been slowing for the second consecutive month, maintaining a deflationary trend of -0.1%. The Ministry of Trade and Integration stated that prices for socially significant goods have increased by 1.8% since the beginning of the year, significantly less than the 8.3% recorded in the same period last year. Agricultural fairs remain an effective tool for price control.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Military Official Detained on Suspicion of Extorting Bribe
item.description: The military prosecutor's office in Kyrgyzstan has detained an official from the Batken district military commissariat on suspicion of extorting a bribe. The official allegedly demanded money from a resident, threatening to send her son for mandatory military service despite a medical exemption. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Food Prices Decline for Second Consecutive Month
item.description: Food prices in Kazakhstan have decreased for the second month in a row, with a deflation rate of 0.1%, according to the Ministry of Trade and Integration. This slowdown is attributed to lower prices for socially significant food items. While overall food prices rose 1.8% year-to-date, this is significantly slower than last year's 8.3% increase.

item.title: Switzerland cooperated with Taliban to deport Afghan refugees: Report
item.description: Swiss officials reportedly cooperated with representatives of Afghanistan's Islamic Emirate in 2025 to identify and deport Afghan nationals. Documents obtained under transparency laws show Swiss officials provided information about individuals scheduled for deportation before interviews. The move has raised concerns about deportee safety and legitimizing the Taliban.

item.title: Tanker Unity with Kazakh Citizen Aboard Towed Closer to Indian Shore Due to Storm
item.description: The tanker Unity, carrying a Kazakh citizen, has been towed closer to the Indian coast near Paradip port due to an approaching storm. The vessel has a broken engine and is in an emergency state. The tanker was previously arrested on May 11 due to financial claims against the shipowner.

item.title: Gay Man from Turkmenistan Recounts Ordeal of Prison, Psychiatric Hospitalization
item.description: A gay man from Turkmenistan, Arslan, shares his harrowing experience of facing charges of 'sodomy,' imprisonment, and forced hospitalization in a psychiatric clinic, along with constant humiliation. He now lives abroad and assists other persecuted LGBT individuals from his home country.

item.title: UN Reports Pakistan Detained 517 Afghan Nationals in One Week
item.description: The International Organization for Migration and UNHCR reported that Pakistani authorities detained 517 Afghan nationals between October 11-17 in Balochistan, Sindh, and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Most detainees lacked documentation. During the same week, 3,883 Afghans returned to Afghanistan, including 499 deportations. Approximately 2.74 million Afghans returned from Pakistan between September 15 and October 17.

item.title: Poland Expresses Interest in Nuclear Cooperation with US and France
item.description: Poland has expressed interest in nuclear cooperation with the United States and France. The country is also considering the construction of a permanent US military base, which could host up to 5,000 American soldiers and cost up to $4.4 billion.

item.title: EAEU Gas Market Development Plan Up for Approval
item.description: The Eurasian Economic Union's gas market development plan until 2030 has been approved by the Council of Heads of Authorized Energy Bodies of EAEU states. The document will be submitted for approval to the Supreme Eurasian Economic Council. Conceptual proposals for amending the legal framework for the formation of the EAEU gas market were also considered.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Four Other Nations Sign Charter for Turkic States' Audit Institutions
item.description: Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkey, and Uzbekistan have signed the charter for the Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions of Turkic States (TURKSAI) in Antalya. The document outlines the principles and operational procedures of the organization, which aims to foster cooperation in state audit, experience sharing, and joint projects among member countries.

item.title: UN Secretary-General Guterres Urges Dialogue and Diplomacy to Prevent Conflict Spread
item.description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has called for efforts to prevent the escalation of conflicts and protect civilians, emphasizing the need for dialogue, diplomacy, and peace. He stated that ending divisive conflicts is crucial to reducing human suffering and that addressing inequalities is essential for building peace. Guterres made these remarks after arriving in Egypt.

item.title: Kazakh President Awards NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang with Dostyk Order of Merit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev awarded NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang the Order of Merit, First Class, during a meeting in Akorda. Tokayev highlighted the significance of Huang's visit in strengthening bilateral cooperation and developing Kazakhstan's artificial intelligence ecosystem. Huang praised Kazakhstan's strategy to become an AI country and proposed it as a global hub for Physical AI.

item.title: Turkmenistan Targets 80 Billion Cubic Meters of Gas Production in 2026, TAPI Deliveries by 2027
item.description: Turkmenistan aims to produce approximately 80 billion cubic meters of natural gas in 2026 and 2027, with plans to increase oil production to eight million metric tons in 2026. Gas deliveries via the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI) pipeline to Afghanistan are targeted for mid-2027, pending Afghan readiness. The country currently supplies 40 billion cubic meters of gas to China and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy Calls for Meaningful Public Participation in Afghanistan's Future
item.description: Afghanistan's UN envoy, Naseer Ahmad Faiq, stressed the need to guarantee meaningful public participation in shaping Afghanistan's future. Speaking at the UN's 81st anniversary, he urged for continued humanitarian aid, defense of women's rights, and efforts towards a peaceful, inclusive Afghanistan that respects international commitments and lives in peace with its neighbors.

item.title: Taliban restrictions hinder women's access to services in western Afghanistan, says OCHA
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reports that Taliban restrictions are significantly impacting women's and girls' access to essential services in western Afghanistan. A recent survey indicated that 90% of aid organizations faced challenges. New Taliban decrees have led to the suspension or closure of 19% of assessed projects.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan presidential election: Businessman Akai Kydyrov intends to run
item.description: Businessman Akai Kydyrov plans to submit documents to participate in the presidential elections in Kyrgyzstan. He has passed the state language proficiency test and intends to apply to the Central Election Commission on October 26. The 35-year-old entrepreneur previously attempted to be elected to the Jogorku Kenesh.

item.title: Taliban home searches in Kabul's Omid-e Sabz township cause fear of property loss
item.description: Residents of Omid-e Sabz township in western Kabul are concerned about repeated home inspections by Taliban delegations, leading to harassment of women and children and a sense of insecurity. Despite approaching dozens of Taliban institutions, residents' concerns remain unaddressed. One resident reported armed Taliban members forcibly entering his home and insulting his family.

item.title: Houthis Attack Al-Makatra Fort in Southern Yemen, Heavy Fighting Reported
item.description: Houthis launched an assault on Al-Makatra fort in Yemen's southern Lahj province. The attack began at 02:00 local time, involving heavy and medium weapons, artillery, and aviation. Government forces attempted to shoot down a reconnaissance drone.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Qatar Explore Investment Cooperation Opportunities, Focus on Education
item.description: Uzbekistan and Qatar are exploring expanded investment cooperation, including Qatari participation in state asset privatization and joint projects in education. Discussions covered real estate privatization in Tashkent and land plots for a new international university.

item.title: UNICEF Warns Afghanistan's Water Crisis is Worsening Due to Multiple Factors
item.description: The UNICEF representative in Afghanistan, Tajuddin Oyewali, has warned that the country's water crisis is intensifying. Factors contributing to this include climate change, rising demand, lack of funding and infrastructure, over-extraction, and ineffective water management. Children and communities across Afghanistan are suffering the consequences of this escalating crisis.

item.title: Uzbek Minister: Social Media Ban for Under-16s Needs More Than Just Law
item.description: Uzbekistan's Digital Technologies Minister Sherzod Shermatov stated that legally restricting social media access for children under 16 requires complementary measures. He emphasized the need for family upbringing, healthy lifestyles, and meaningful leisure activities. While technology offers educational benefits, risks like excessive screen time, poor diet, and inactivity, impacting children's health, must be addressed.

item.title: Tajikistan Begins Reconstruction of Vakhdat-Obi Garm Highway
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon has laid the foundation stone for the reconstruction of the Vakhdat-Obi Garm highway. The 70-kilometer road project is expected to be completed in 18 months. The reconstruction includes building pedestrian paths, installing road signs, and safety barriers. The project is co-financed by the government and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.

item.title: Chinese Company Plans Entry into Uzbekistan's Taxi Market
item.description: A Chinese company intends to enter the Uzbek taxi market by launching 5,000 vehicles and its own application, according to the First Deputy Minister of Transport. The company's name and launch date were not disclosed, but it is expected to be a new player in the market soon. This news comes amid disruptions in Yandex Go services across Central Asia.

item.title: Aid Agencies Request $12.8 Million for Non-Food Needs in Afghanistan This Winter
item.description: Aid organizations are seeking $12.8 million to address non-food needs, including shelter and winter supplies, for vulnerable populations in Afghanistan. The funds will support 198,832 individuals in 102 priority districts from October 2026 to March 2027. This appeal comes amid a severe funding shortfall for humanitarian programs in the country.

item.title: Kazakhstan Notifies Russia of Suspension of Sunflower Seed Imports
item.description: Kazakhstan has informed Russia's Rosselkhoznadzor of its intention to suspend sunflower seed imports due to the detection of Phomopsis in numerous shipments. Since October 23, 2026, phytosanitary certificates for sunflower seeds from Russia to Kazakhstan will be temporarily halted to prevent the spread of quarantine objects.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses Ways to Increase Pension Amounts
item.description: Discussions have been held in Kazakhstan regarding methods to increase pension amounts. The specific details or outcomes of these discussions were not provided in the source text. The focus appears to be on exploring potential strategies for enhancing retirement benefits within the country.

item.title: Humanitarian Organizations to Support Economic Inclusion of Afghan Returnees
item.description: Millions of Afghans returning from Iran and Pakistan face challenges finding employment, housing, and services. Humanitarian organizations, including IOM and UNDP, are working to support their economic inclusion. The International Organization for Migration reported 6.04 million returns between September 2023 and May 2026, straining resources in Afghanistan.

item.title: Taliban Intensifies Dismissal of Former Prosecutors, Replacing Them with Fighters
item.description: Former prosecutors from the previous Afghan government are being dismissed and replaced by Taliban fighters, reportedly on the verbal order of leader Hibatullah Akhundzada. A letter shows 11 former prosecutors in six provinces were dismissed without stated reasons. Sources claim fabricated corruption cases against Taliban officials prompted the dismissals.

item.title: Iran Reportedly Escalating Efforts to Assassinate US Officials Abroad
item.description: An intelligence memo obtained by Axios indicates Iran has significantly increased efforts to target US officials outside the United States, with some plots reaching advanced stages. US officials cited these concerns as a reason for reducing embassy staffing in the Middle East.

item.title: Russia Recruits Around 1,400 Tajik Citizens for War in Ukraine in First Nine Months of 2026
item.description: Russia has involved approximately 1,400 Tajik citizens in the war against Ukraine in the first nine months of 2026, according to the Ukrainian project 'I Want to Live'. As of October 1, 2026, 20,437 Central Asian nationals were involved, with 5,308 from Tajikistan. Tajikistan ranks second among Central Asian countries in terms of citizens involved.

item.title: Tashkent Air Quality Reaches "Very Unhealthy" Levels in Some Areas
item.description: Tashkent's air quality has reached "very unhealthy" levels in certain areas. The deterioration occurred overnight between October 23rd and 24th, attributed to falling temperatures, weak winds, and temperature inversions.

item.title: Five Children Rescued from Apartment Fire in Karaganda
item.description: Eight people, including five children, were rescued by emergency services from a fire in a residential building in Karaganda. Another seven residents were evacuated. No injuries were reported. The fire involved furniture and belongings on the fourth floor of a nine-story building.

item.title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Visits Kazakhstan, Discusses AI Nation Strategy
item.description: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang made his first visit to Kazakhstan, meeting with the Minister of Digital Development. Huang stated that Kazakhstan is the first country he has visited where the president has declared an intention to transform the nation into an AI nation. He believes AI will elevate Kazakhstan's economy and create new opportunities for citizens and companies.

item.title: Three-Year-Old Girl Falls into Coma After Dental Treatment in Pavlodar
item.description: A three-year-old girl in Pavlodar has fallen into a coma following dental treatment, confirmed by the regional health department. Relatives reported the child experienced breathing difficulties during the procedure. The clinic stated they follow all medical protocols, while the girl remains in intensive care.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes Medal in Honor of Gaziz Baitasov
item.description: Kazakhstan has established a departmental medal of the Ministry of Internal Affairs named after Gaziz Baitasov. The award, initiated by the President, will recognize law enforcement officers for courage and heroism in the line of duty. The first medal was presented to Baitasov's wife. Gaziz Baitasov, a police captain, died in 2011 while apprehending a terrorist.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Health Ministry Opposes 'Tips' for Medical Workers
item.description: The Ministry of Health of Kyrgyzstan has spoken out against the practice of monetary gratitude for medical workers, even if patients wish to pay through official channels. An official stated that doctors' salaries have been increased since April 2026, making them sufficient. The ministry believes that even voluntary monetary tips could negatively impact the healthcare system over time.

item.title: Akmzhan Festival Gathers Top Agrarians of Kyzylorda Region
item.description: The 'Akmzhan' agro-cultural festival in the Kyzylorda region concluded with the 'Golden Autumn - 2026' ceremony, honoring the best agricultural workers. The region allocated 37 billion tenge for agricultural support this year, a 1.5-fold increase from the previous year. Production in the sector reached 178 billion tenge in nine months.

item.title: State Awards Presented in Atyrau on Kazakhstan's Republic Day
item.description: On the eve of Republic Day, the Akim of Atyrau region, Bolat Akchulakov, presented state awards on behalf of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev to citizens who contributed to the country's development. The awards recognized individuals from various sectors including industry, energy, agriculture, education, and culture.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Second Month of Declining Food Prices, Government Reports
item.description: Food prices in Kazakhstan have decreased for the second consecutive month, according to the government. While the monthly decline is 0.1%, year-to-date prices for socially significant goods have risen by 1.8%. Some vegetables have seen price increases due to colder weather, prompting plans for producer agreements and more agricultural fairs.
